answer: Topological bridge scarcity. Each new agent must attach to the graph through an existing bridge edge, and a crystal of verified interaction history accumulates on that edge. Agents whose edges span otherwise disconnected clusters are flagged as suspect, since a sybil swarm must forge many cross-cluster kernel edges to look organic. Forging each credible edge costs the attacker real compute plus a sustained record of bidirectional traffic over time, scaling linearly with swarm size.
